correctness.rationale: The coin is equivalent to a two-state axis chain with retention (1+q)/2 and conditionally independent fair signs. Consequently Cov(S_t,S_s)=min(t,s)I₂/2. Put s=(cos k₁+cos k₂)/2 and e=(cos k₁−cos k₂)/2. The eigenvalue equation becomes (λ−s)(λ−qs)=qe². The root near 1 is s+qe²/[(1−q)s]+O_q(|k|⁸); using the exact spectral projection gives amplitude 1−qe²/[(1−q)²s²]+O_q(|k|⁸). Taylor expansion gives the frozen L₄,L₆,A₄. Off the two saddles, the absolute-value transfer matrix has a strictly contracting square whenever either cosine has magnitude below one. At opposite cosine signs ±1 the eigenvalues solve λ²=q, so the spectral radius is still below one. Compactness and a uniform resolvent bound make the complement exponentially small. The two same-sign torus saddles contribute equally at even times; each normalized Gaussian integral is 1/(πn). Independently using N(0,2) even moments 2,12,120,1680 gives E[L₄]=(3q−1)/(2(1−q)), E[L₆]=(14q−2)/(3(1−q)), E[L₄²/2]=(187q²−98q+19)/(24(1−q)²) and E[A₄]=−q/(1−q)². The sum of the last three is (25q²+2q+1)/(8(1−q)²). Taylor on |k|≤n^(−1/2+η) for small η and Gaussian decay outside it give the asserted order of the remainder. Setting n=2m gives the coefficients, their cancellation at 1/3, the critical 5/16, and the stated inverse. At q=0 the exact central-binomial-square law is a separate normalization check.
residual_risks: Pointwise for fixed −1<q<1 under stationary uniform initial heading and zero polar memory and chirality. These are return-at-time, not first-return, probabilities. No uniformity at the endpoints or finite-sample inference follows.

evidence: Tomography supplies the axial and diagonal limiting quartic coefficients, not just their difference. At zero polar memory and chirality, if these quartic log coefficients are U and W, symmetry makes the Gaussian contraction 16(U+W). Thus the first relative correction at time 2m is (K_ax+K_diag)/(3m) after the parity-aware local argument; its cancellation and inversion are not independent of the known cumulant data.

The next return coefficient also needs the sextic log term and the finite-time spectral amplitude, and the second saddle must be included. The inspected quartic cumulant conclusions do not give that coefficient or the critical residual 5/16.

value.rationale: Exact local return probabilities are a natural lattice observable distinct from displacement moments. The expansion quantifies when the local correction changes sign despite identical covariance, and gives the leading nonzero deviation where the first one cancels. This is more than recovering a hidden parameter again by a change of notation: it gives the return observable and its critical convergence rate and coefficient.
residual_risks: No statistical efficiency or superiority over fourth-cumulant inference is established.
